From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

As of 2018, Davies has 86 professional wins worldwide, with 20 on the [LPGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LPGA_Tour), including four [majors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_majors).<sup>[6]</sup> From 1985 to 2010, she won at least one individual title somewhere in the world every season, except for 2005, and was the first golfer, male or female, to win tournaments on five continents in one year. She is a member of U.S.-based LPGA Tour and a life member of the Ladies European Tour.<sup>[7]</sup> She was inducted into the [World Golf Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Golf_Hall_of_Fame) in 2015.<sup>[8]</sup>
For other people with similar names, see [Laura Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Davis_%28disambiguation%29).
Amateur career [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laura_Davies&action=edit&section=1)

**Dame Laura Jane Davies** (born 5 October 1963) is an English [professional golfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_golfer). She has achieved the status of her nation's most accomplished female golfer of modern times,<sup>[2][3]</sup> being the second non-American to finish at the top of the LPGA money list<sup>[2]</sup> as well as winning the [Ladies European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladies_European_Tour) (LET) Order of Merit a record seven times: in 1985, 1986, 1992, 1996, 1999, 2004 and 2006.<sup>[4][5]</sup>

A native of [Coventry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coventry), Davies began as an amateur international player for Great Britain, compiling a notable record. She was the 1983 English Intermediate Champion, the 1984 [Welsh Ladies Open Stroke Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Ladies_Open_Stroke_Play_Championship)

Professional career [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laura_Davies&action=edit&section=2)
Ladies European Tour [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laura_Davies&action=edit&section=3)

Davies turned professional in 1985. She started her professional career on the WPGET (now [Ladies European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladies_European_Tour)) in 1985 when she won both [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LET_Rookie_of_the_Year) and [Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LET_Order_of_Merit) titles.<sup>[4]</sup> She subsequently won the [Sports Journalists' Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Journalists'_Association) Peter Wilson Trophy as International Newcomer of the Year 1985.<sup>[11]</sup> She repeated the Order of Merit win in 1986 having won four titles, one of which was the [Women's British Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_British_Open) (prior to it becoming a major).<sup>[4][12]</sup>

In 1987, she went to the United States and won the [U.S. Women's Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Women's_Open) in an 18-hole playoff against [Ayako Okamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayako_Okamoto) and [JoAnne Carner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JoAnne_Carner). It was a victory that led the LPGA to amend its constitution. Davies was not a member of the LPGA Tour, so the LPGA changed its constitution to grant Davies automatic membership.<sup>[13]</sup> Davies became the third non-U.S. citizen and the second European player, after [Catherine Lacoste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Lacoste) in [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_U.S._Women's_Open), to win the U.S. Women's Open. For six days, Davies was holder of both the U.S and British Open titles. The 1987 Women's British Open took place the week after the U.S. Women's Open and in her defence Davies finished tied second, one shot behind winner [Alison Nicholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Nicholas).<sup>[4]</sup>

Tour and once in Japan, becoming the first woman ever to win on all three major Tours in the same year. <sup>[2]</sup>

Her four consecutive victories at the [J Golf Phoenix LPGA International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Golf_Phoenix_LPGA_International) between 1994 and 1997 made Davies the first LPGA player to win the same tournament in four consecutive years.<sup>[14]</sup>

In 1994, she was the first golfer, male or female, to win on five different golf tours in one calendar year: US, Europe, Asia, Japan and Australia.<sup>[4][15]</sup> and became the first European player to be ranked unofficial number one in the world on the Ping Leaderboard.<sup>[2]</sup> In 1996, she was again ranked number one on the Ping leaderboard.

In 2004 Davies was the first woman to compete in the men's [European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour), entering the ANZ Championship in [Sydney, Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney,_Australia), playing from the same tees as the men.[16][17] She failed to make the cut, finishing second to last. She beat the LPGA Tour record for most eagles in a season, scoring 19 during the 2004 season.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]

Solheim Cup and other team appearances [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laura_Davies&action=edit&section=5)

In [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Solheim_Cup), she was a member of the inaugural European [Solheim Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solheim_Cup) Team. She returned as part of every European team through 2011. Davies is the only player to participate in the first 12 [Solheim Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solheim_Cup) matches on either the United States or European side.<sup>[18]</sup> Davies is the all-time leader in points won in the Solheim Cup, breaking the record of [Annika Sörenstam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annika_S%C3%B6renstam) by winning a Saturday fourballs match partnered by [Melissa Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa_Reid) on 24 September 2011.<sup>[19]</sup> Davies went on to increase her record point total to 25 by halving her singles match with [Juli Inkster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli_Inkster) on 25 September 2011, as the Europeans captured the Solheim Cup for the fourth time.<sup>[20]</sup> She was appointed as non-playing assistant captain for the European teams at the [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Solheim_Cup), [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Solheim_Cup) and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Solheim_Cup) Solheim Cup tournaments.<sup>[21][22]</sup>
Davies was part of the LPGA team at the Wendy's 3-Tour Challenge three times between 1994 and 1996.<sup>[23]</sup>

Davies also was part of a mixed team event of [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour) and [LPGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LPGA_Tour) players at the [JCPenney Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JCPenney_Classic) four times between 1996 and 1999.<sup>[24][25]</sup> Davies won the event in 1999 alongside [John Daly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Daly_%28golfer%29).<sup>[26]</sup>

She represented England at the [Women's World Cup of Golf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_World_Cup_of_Golf) in 2000 (with [Trish Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trish_Johnson) when winning individually),<sup>[27]</sup> 2005 (with [Karen Stupples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Stupples)),<sup>[28]</sup> 2006 (with Kirsty Taylor)<sup>[29]</sup> and 2007 (with Trish Johnson).<sup>[30]</sup> She was a Captain's pick for the International Team at the 2006 [Lexus Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus_Cup).<sup>[31]</sup>
